scenario.name: Microsoft WinRM, CrowdStrike & SigmaHQ DFIR — WinRM / WS-Management Lateral Movement & wsmprovhost.exe Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a corporate office tower linked by a fast pneumatic canister-tube system built for remote IT administration. An intruder sitting at an ordinary desk drops a sealed command canister down the tube to a database server, where the receiving dock opens a dedicated remote-command bench and executes every instruction inside while both sending and receiving ledgers stamp detailed receipts of the canister and every line of code run. In this scenario (T1021.006, Microsoft WinRM, CrowdStrike & SigmaHQ DFIR, WinRM / WS-Management Lateral Movement & wsmprovhost.exe Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: outbound WSMan Session Initialization, then destination Server WSMan Shell Creation, then wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Outbound WSMan Session Initialization, then Destination Server WSMan Shell Creation, then wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Outbound WSMan Session Initialization on Source Host (WinRM EventID 142 & 6)
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1021.006 - Remote Services: Windows Remote Management)
stages.description: At the originating workstation, the intruder loads an automated script into a sealed remote-administration canister and launches it through the campus pneumatic tube toward the target database server, leaving an outbound dispatch ticket in the local tube log. When the attacker runs Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV-SQL01 -ScriptBlock { ... } on the source workstation, Microsoft-Windows-WinRM/Operational on the source host logs EventID 6 (Creating WSMan session) showing the exact destination connection URI (http://SRV-SQL01:5985/wsman?PSVersion=5.1) (logged in WinEvent Event 6 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-WinRM/Operational , Source Host, EventID=6 , Creating WSMan Session, TargetConnectionUri=http://SRV-SQL01.corp.local:5985/wsman so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV-SQL01.corp.local -ScriptBlock { procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Temp\sql.dmp } (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1021.006 during "Outbound WSMan Session Initialization on Source Host , WinRM EventID 142 & 6" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact Source WinRM/Operational EventID 6: Creating WSMan session to connection http://SRV-SQL01.corp.local:5985/wsman runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Source WinRM/Operational EventID 6: Creating WSMan session to connection http://SRV-SQL01.co so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.006 during "Outbound WSMan Session Initialization on Source Host , WinRM EventID 142 & 6" , When the attacker runs Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV-SQL01 -ScriptBlock { while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Invoke-Command -ComputerName SRV-SQL01.corp.local -ScriptBlock { ... } / ⇠#1 ACK 6) from Node ① (#1 Source Host (Invoke-Command)) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 wsmprovhost.exe Host Process).

stages.title: Stage 2: Destination Server WSMan Shell Creation (WinRM EventID 91 & Security EventID 4624 Type 3)
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1021.006 - Destination WinRM EventID 91 Shell Creation)
stages.description: When the canister pops into the receiving tube at the database server, the front door receptionist stamps the visitor network arrival pass and immediately opens a freshly numbered remote workbench slot for the incoming session. On destination server SRV-SQL01, HTTP.sys receives the SOAP POST /wsman request on port 5985. Security logs EventID 4624 (LogonType 3 Network), and Microsoft-Windows-WinRM/Operational logs EventID 91 (Creating WSMan shell on server with ResourceUri http://schemas.microsoft.com/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell and clientIP 10.10.4.15) (logged in WinEvent Event 91 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-WinRM/Operational , Destination Host, EventID=91 , Creating WSMan Shell, ResourceUri=http://schemas.microsoft.com/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell, ClientIp=10.10.4.15 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Destination WinRM/Operational EventID 91: Creating WSMan shell with ResourceUri http://schemas.microsoft.com/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell (clientIP: 10.10.4.15) (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1021.006 during "Destination Server WSMan Shell Creation , WinRM EventID 91 & Security EventID 4624 Type 3" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact Destination PowerShell/Operational EventID 400 / 40961: HostName=ServerRemoteHost runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1021.006 during "Destination Server WSMan Shell Creation , WinRM EventID 91 & Security EventID 4624 Type 3" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ svchost.exe -k NetworkService -s WinRM (Creating WSMan shell for CORP\admin_ops) / ⇠#2 ACK 91) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 HTTP.sys /wsman (:5985/:5986)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 wsmprovhost.exe Host Process).

stages.title: Stage 3: wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning & ServerRemoteHost ScriptBlock Logging (Sysmon EID 1 & PS 4104)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059.001 - wsmprovhost.exe Parentage & ServerRemoteHost)
stages.description: Inside the newly opened workbench slot, a dedicated remote-host clerk wakes up to run the intruder commands and child utilities, while the room built-in security camera records the full verbatim transcript of every single script block executed. The WinRM service spawns the WS-Management Provider Host (C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding), which initializes the PowerShell runspace (HostName=ServerRemoteHost) and spawns any external binaries invoked by the attacker script block (Sysmon EventID 1 with ParentImage=wsmprovhost.exe) (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe, ChildImage=C:\Users\Public\procdump64.exe, PowerShellHostName=ServerRemoteHost so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -> Image=C:\Users\Public\procdump64.exe (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -> Image=C:\Users\Public\p so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1059.001 during "wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning & ServerRemoteHost ScriptBlock Logging , Sysmon EID 1 & PS 4104" , The WinRM service spawns the WS-Management Provider Host , C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Windows PowerShell EventID 400: HostName=ServerRemoteHost HostApplication=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1059.001 during "wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning & ServerRemoteHost ScriptBlock Logging , Sysmon EID 1 & PS 4104" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ C:\Users\Public\procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Temp\sql.dmp / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 HTTP.sys /wsman (:5985/:5986)) to Node ④ (#4 svchost.exe (WinRM Service)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 wsmprovhost.exe Host Process).

steps.simpleExplanation: The WinRM service spawns the WS-Management Provider Host (C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding), which initializes the PowerShell runspace (HostName=ServerRemoteHost) and spawns any external binaries invoked by the attacker script block (Sysmon EventID 1 with ParentImage=wsmprovhost.exe) (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe, ChildImage=C:\Users\Public\procdump64.exe, PowerShellHostName=ServerRemoteHost so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -> Image=C:\Users\Public\procdump64.exe (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -> Image=C:\Users\Public\p so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1059.001 during "wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning & ServerRemoteHost ScriptBlock Logging , Sysmon EID 1 & PS 4104" , The WinRM service spawns the WS-Management Provider Host , C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Windows PowerShell EventID 400: HostName=ServerRemoteHost HostApplication=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1059.001 during "wsmprovhost.exe Child Process Spawning & ServerRemoteHost ScriptBlock Logging , Sysmon EID 1 & PS 4104" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 1 (recording EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\wsmprovhost.exe, ChildImage=C:\Users\Public\procdump64.exe, PowerShellHostName=ServerRemoteHost under T1059.001): Hunt for Sysmon EventID 1 events where ParentImage ends with \wsmprovhost.exe or \winrsHost.exe, and correlate with PowerShell EventID 4104 executed within the same timeframe.
